note: XVIII: Renfield's appeal on long and establishing shots only (Ian, 18 Nov).
style: A cinematic Romantic oil painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, atmospheric haze, cool blue moonlight against warm amber lamplight, a wide view, rich painterly brushwork. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Close view at night: a lantern standing on the bare boards of an asylum cell floor, and the long black shadows of five standing men stretched across the whitewashed wall. No faces.

A long asylum corridor at four in the morning, 1893: at the far end an attendant dozing on a wooden chair under a turned-down gas jet, one cell door ajar with warm light spilling out. Any people are small, far off or in shadow, with no detail in their faces.

Exterior at four in the morning seen from the grounds of the old house Carfax: across the high wall, the dark asylum with one barred ground-floor window glowing, the moon low behind bare trees, mist in the hollows. No people.

Seen through the iron grille of a cell door from the dark corridor: inside, a lamplit whitewashed cell and the silhouettes of several men standing, a thin man in the middle with his hands raised. Any people are small, far off or in shadow, with no detail in their faces.
